risk_assessment.rationale: The command line shows an obfuscated PowerShell payload that resolves only to a benign Git status operation.  However, the event correlates with 87 other lateral‑movement hits, is executed from an npm module under a user account with unfamiliar internal domain names, and carries an explicit obfuscation flag.  No clear malicious payload or exfiltration activity was detected, so the risk is assessed as medium: suspicious enough to merit analyst review but not yet actionable for immediate containment.

recommended_actions: Escalate to a human analyst for manual review
Review the parent-child process execution tree for the affected host
recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Perform an integrity check on the @anthropic‑ai/claude-code package that is being executed by node.exe – verify its hash against the official npm registry and inspect any recent commits for suspicious changes.
Audit the user profile (C:\Users\tommy.wong) for other anomalous scripts or scheduled tasks that might be leveraging node.js to launch PowerShell in an encoded form.

Capture a full packet trace from the host during the next execution of this command line to confirm whether any outbound connections are made to the internal domains listed (dev‑twong02.victimcorp.com, tommy.wong, cli.js) or to external IPs that could indicate data exfiltration.
Enable detailed Sysmon logging for child processes spawned by node.exe and correlate with other lateral‑movement indicators such as SMB shares, remote desktop sessions, or credential dumping tools.
If the package is found to be compromised, roll back to a known good version or remove it entirely from the environment until a clean replacement can be installed.
triage_rationale_experimental: The encoded PowerShell command resolves to a benign git status call, yet its execution via node.exe and strong correlation with lateral‑movement indicators raise suspicion; without evidence of malicious payload or exfiltration, the alert remains inconclusive and warrants analyst review.
